patient.name: Marcus Whitfield
patient.chiefComplaint: Burn to right forearm, severe pain

history.hpi: Patient was cooking in his kitchen when a grease-filled pan flared up and splashed hot grease onto his right forearm. His spouse ran cool water over the area for a few minutes before EMS arrival. He reports immediate, severe burning pain that has not improved, rated 9 out of 10. Denies loss of consciousness, denies other injuries, denies any facial or airway involvement.
history.lastOralIntake: Lunch approximately 1 hour prior to the incident
history.events: Grease fire flare-up while cooking; spouse called 911 immediately after cooling the burn with water

scene.dispatch: 41-year-old male, burn injury, residence, conscious and breathing
scene.location: Single-family home, kitchen, patient seated at the kitchen table holding his right arm
scene.safety: Stove burner off, no active fire, small grease spill on floor near stove - slip hazard
scene.bystanders: Spouse present, witnessed the flare-up and cooled the burn with water before EMS arrival
visualCues: Reddened, blistered partial-thickness burn to right forearm, approximately 4-5% TBSA
Blisters intact, wound moist with mottled pink-white appearance
No soot, singed hair, or facial involvement
Patient guarding right arm against his chest, grimacing, rocking in chair

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 41-year-old male seated at his kitchen table, guarding a visibly burned right forearm. He is alert, oriented, and in severe distress from pain.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong and regular
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all extremities; guarding right forearm
otherFindings: Partial-thickness burn to right forearm, ~4-5% TBSA, blisters intact
No airway, facial, or circumferential involvement
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It hurts so bad, please do something, it's burning!"

transitions.condition: Crew performs burn wound care (stop the burning, dry dressing, TBSA/pain assessment), establishes IV access avoiding burned skin, and administers weight-based fentanyl for severe pain.
Crew addresses the wound but does not establish IV access or administer analgesia despite the patient's reported 9/10 pain.

phases.name: Burn cared for, fentanyl given
phases.description: Crew completes burn wound care, establishes IV access on unburned skin, and administers weight-based IV fentanyl for severe pain, applying capnography to monitor for opioid-related hypoventilation.
phases.triggerCondition: After stopping the burning process and covering the wound with a dry dressing, the crew reassesses the patient's pain at 9/10 and proceeds with IV access and weight-based fentanyl analgesia per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong and regular
otherFindings: Right forearm covered with dry dressing, jewelry removed
IV established in left forearm, avoiding burn site
Pain improved to 5/10 after initial fentanyl dose
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That's a little better, but it still really hurts."

expectedActions.shortAction: Stop the burning: remove jewelry and any non-adherent wet clothing from right forearm
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Stop the burning: Remove wet clothing (if not stuck to the patient); Remove jewelry; Leave blisters intact
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing contact with wet clothing or constricting jewelry continues tissue damage and can cause swelling complications.

expectedActions.shortAction: Cover burn with dry, clean dressing; do not apply gels or ointments
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Minimize burn wound contamination: Cover burns with dry dressing or clean sheet. Do not apply gels or ointments
expectedActions.rationale: Dry coverage reduces contamination risk and pain from air exposure without interfering with burn center evaluation.

expectedActions.shortAction: Estimate TBSA (~4-5%) via Rule of Nines and document baseline pain score of 9/10
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Estimate TBSA burned and depth of burn Use "Rule of 9's" Document pain scale
expectedActions.rationale: TBSA and pain documentation guide transport destination decisions and track treatment effectiveness.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access on unburned skin (left forearm), avoiding the burned right forearm
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access, avoid placement through burned skin
expectedActions.rationale: IV placement through burned tissue risks infection and unreliable access.

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 90 mcg IV (90 kg × 1 mcg/kg = 90 mcg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For Moderate to Severe pain, analgesics include: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Weight-based fentanyl controls severe burn pain rated 9/10 while remaining under the protocol maximum initial dose.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply waveform capnography to monitor for early hypoventilation after opioid administration
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Use of non-invasive capnography is an earlier predictor of hypoventilation than pulse oximetry if opioid medications are administered
expectedActions.rationale: Capnography detects opioid-induced hypoventilation before pulse oximetry desaturation occurs.

transitions.condition: Five minutes after the initial dose, reassessment shows pain remains above 4/10 with stable vital signs, meeting criteria to repeat the fentanyl dose before transport.

phases.name: Pain reassessed, repeat fentanyl given
phases.description: Pain remains significant on reassessment, so a repeat weight-based fentanyl dose is given per protocol. Pain improves and the patient is transported in a position of comfort with continued monitoring.
phases.triggerCondition: Five minutes after the initial fentanyl dose, the patient's pain remains at 5/10 with stable vital signs, meeting protocol criteria for a repeat dose prior to transport.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong and regular
otherFindings: Pain improved to 2/10 after repeat fentanyl dose
No signs of hypoventilation, EtCO2 within normal range
Packaged for transport in position of comfort
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Wow, that's a lot better, thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Repeat fentanyl 90 mcg IV (90 kg × 1 mcg/kg = 90 mcg) 5 minutes after first dose for persistent pain
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If indicated based on pain assessment, and vital signs allow, repeat pain medication administration (excluding acetaminophen and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory medicines) after 5 minutes of the previous dose
expectedActions.rationale: Persistent pain above 4/10 with stable vitals meets protocol criteria to repeat the weight-based dose.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess pain score and vital signs; transport in position of comfort
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Transport in position of comfort and reassess as indicated
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing reassessment confirms analgesic effectiveness and detects any adverse response en route.

phases.name: Pain management delayed
phases.description: The crew addresses the burn wound but does not establish IV access or administer fentanyl, leaving the patient's severe pain unmanaged. He becomes increasingly anxious and tachycardic.
phases.triggerCondition: Despite reported 9/10 pain, the crew does not establish IV access or administer analgesia, leaving the burn pain unmanaged.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, strong and rapid
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all extremities; guarding right forearm, restless
otherFindings: No IV access established, no analgesia given
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "Please, it still hurts so bad, isn't there something you can give me?"

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize unmanaged severe pain (9/10); establish IV access and give fentanyl 90 mcg IV per protocol
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: For Moderate to Severe pain, analgesics include: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Correcting the delay restores appropriate pain control and prevents escalating physiologic stress from untreated severe pain.
